description: Learn about the jobs a computer does with information. Practice matching simple questions about computer parts, saved work, and devices that do more than one job.

questionVariants: What does input mean for a computer?
Which way does information go during input?
What happens when a computer gets input?
answerVariants: Information or directions go into the computer.
The computer takes in information or directions.
Information comes in for the computer to use.

questionVariants: How can a sensor tell how warm a room is?
What does a sensor do to learn about the air?
How can a sensor check a room without someone typing?
answerVariants: It measures the air and sends the reading to a computer.
It checks how warm the air is and sends that number.
It checks how warm the air is and tells a computer.

questionVariants: What does processing mean?
What happens during processing?
How does processing use the information a computer gets?
answerVariants: The computer follows steps to work with the information.
The computer uses directions to do work with information.
The computer works with information by following steps.

questionVariants: What do the letters CPU stand for?
What is the full name of the chip called the CPU?
How do you say CPU without using the three letters?
answerVariants: Central processing unit.
The central processing unit.
Its full name is central processing unit.

questionVariants: Why might a computer have extra chips besides its CPU?
How can extra chips help the main chip?
What kind of work can other chips do to help the CPU?
answerVariants: They can do one special kind of job.
They can help by doing a certain kind of task.
They can take on a special task they were made to do.

concepts.conceptName: RAM Holds Work Being Used Now
questionVariants: What does RAM hold while you use a computer?
How does RAM help with the work you are doing now?
What is RAM used for during a task?
answerVariants: It holds the information and steps being used right now.
It keeps the current information and steps ready to use.
It is a fast work space for information and steps in use now.

questionVariants: What does storage keep when a computer is turned off?
How does storage keep your saved work when the power is off?
What stays in storage after you shut down a computer?
answerVariants: It keeps saved files and programs for later.
Saved files and programs stay there for another day.
It holds saved work and programs, even with the power off.

questionVariants: What does output mean for a computer?
Which way do results go during output?
What happens when a computer gives output?
answerVariants: The computer sends out a result, like a picture, sound, or movement.
A result comes out as information or an action.
The computer gives a result that can be seen, heard, or used.

concepts.conceptName: A Buzz Can Be a Message
questionVariants: How can a device send you a message you feel?
How does a device give a signal through touch?
How can a device let you feel a signal instead of seeing or hearing it?
answerVariants: A small motor makes a buzz you can feel.
A tiny motor makes the device shake a little.
A little motor makes a shaking signal you feel.

questionVariants: What two jobs does a touchscreen do?
How does a touchscreen both take in and give out information?
Why does a touchscreen count as both input and output?
answerVariants: It senses your finger taps and shows words or pictures.
It notices where you touch and shows things you can see.
It takes in your taps and gives you words and pictures to look at.

concepts.conceptName: A Network Part Sends and Gets Messages
questionVariants: What two jobs does a network part do with messages?
How does a network part move messages both ways?
Why can a network part be both input and output?
answerVariants: It gets messages from other computers and sends messages to them.
It sends messages out to other computers and gets messages back.
It takes in messages from other computers and sends messages out.

concepts.conceptName: Saving Puts In and Opening Takes Out
questionVariants: What happens to information when you save a file and open it later?
How does information move when you save your work and then open it?
What two things happen in a drive when you save and later open a file?
answerVariants: Saving puts information in the drive. Opening gets it back out.
The information goes into the drive when saved and comes back out when opened.
The drive takes in the file when you save it and gives it back when you open it.

concepts.conceptName: A Job Depends on the Task
questionVariants: How do you tell which job a device is doing?
What should you check before calling a device input or output?
Why can a device have a different job in a new task?
answerVariants: Look at what it does with information in that task.
Follow the information and check what the device is doing now.
Its job depends on how it uses information in the task.
